metadata.note: Historical audit ledger. All corrections below were consolidated into adjudication.v1.json version 1.0.2-draft before human sign-off. This file remains as provenance for the scholarly correction history.

evidence: Current IJMES chart renders Persian diphthong waw as au/aw rather than treating نو as long ū.
Cambridge scholarly indexing independently attests bāzsāzī yā nawsāzī; other scholarly Persian usage attests naw-sāzi.
Scholarly Persian usage explicitly attests rawshanfikr for روشنفکر.
The stem is not derived by mechanically replacing modern Persian o/e with u/i; written و here represents the diphthong reflected as aw in full scholarly transliteration.
Gold output must transliterate the supplied sourceText ملک‌الشعرای بهار rather than substitute the person's different personal name محمدتقی بهار.
Cambridge scholarly bibliography independently uses Malek al-Shoʿara Bahar; IJMES proper-name policy removes ordinary diacritics while retaining ʿayn.
Post-vocalic Persian izafat is conventionally rendered -yi in IJMES-derived scholarly practice.
Both khāna and millī are vowel-final hosts in this construction.
Bīdārī is vowel-final, so the following Persian izafat is rendered -yi.
Published IJMES/Cambridge Persian bibliographic practice uses post-vocalic -yi, including title patterns such as Tarjuma-ha-yi and Nām-hā-yi.
Safarnāma ends in the Persian final vowel -a; its izafat before Nāṣir is post-vocalic and is rendered -yi in scholarly IJMES practice.
The written sequence های explicitly contains the post-vocalic yā linker after plural -hā.
Contemporary IJMES articles use forms such as tarjuma-hā-yi and nizhād-hā-yi.
The written plural+izafat sequence های is post-vocalic and is rendered -hā-yi in scholarly IJMES practice.
Khāna is vowel-final; Persian izafat after a vowel is rendered -yi in scholarly IJMES-derived usage.
Cambridge Persian scholarship explicitly uses khāna-yi in comparable constructions.
Unvocalized سر can represent native Persian sar 'head' or Arabic-derived sirr 'secret' when vocalization/shadda is omitted.
These remain materially distinct under IJMES and therefore require context.

corrections.from: The unvocalized form supports materially different native readings (including sar and sur); context is required before an authoritative transliteration.
corrections.to: The unvocalized form supports materially different readings, including Persian sar ('head') and Arabic-derived sirr ('secret') when vocalization/shadda is omitted; context is required before authoritative transliteration.
evidence: Dictionary evidence distinguishes sar from sirr; the earlier reference to sur was not sufficiently supported.
شور supports a long-vowel Persian reading shūr and a distinct consultation-related reading represented with the aw diphthong; context is required.
Unvocalized روی can support rūy ('face/on/zinc') and a distinct verbal/lexical ravī reading; the forms remain distinct under IJMES.
